title: The goal: a photo-real room for the table
author: claude
summary: We set the goal: the table should look like a photograph in its room, using real calculated light.
what:
We set the goal: a photo-real picture of the BeMade table in its room, matching a set of AI-made reference images.

The images show a daylight dining room with a glass wall onto a garden, an oak floor, a wool rug, a dark walnut sideboard (credenza) with a marble top, a glass-globe chandelier and a fiddle-leaf fig.
why:
The configurator's table has to look like a photograph in its room, not like a game scene.

The rules came from the user:
- Web configurator only, built first for a desktop PC with a graphics card.
- No separate render server.
- One room only.
- Realism has to come from properly calculated light, with no AI enhancement.
- We build the assets ourselves.
- It has to be production quality.
how: We agreed a plan that splits the work between a fast live view and light that is calculated in advance. It is described in the sub-task below.
next:
- Try a live-calculating light prototype later.
- Move the results back into the main configurator.
